facet1 =~ A+F+S+G
  facet2 =~ F+S+G

What is the difference between these facets?  They have the same 3 indicators, and Facet 1 has an additional 4th indicator.  That does not seem like enough to identify them as unique factors, so I think the only reason this model even converges on a solution is because you set "orthogonal = TRUE" (which contradicts the covariance between facets in your diagram).  I'm not sure what role the interaction between facets would play in your model because it is missing from your diagram, but it might complicate identification issues if you just expect the facets to have an interaction effect on their indicators.
I have no idea about how to specify the interaction between facet1 and facet2.

The product-indicator approach only works for defining first-order constructs (because you would need to calculate products among observed variables, not latent variables).  So I think you would have to use the latent moderated structures (LMS) approach, which is implemented in Mplus and the R package "nlsem", but not lavaan.
